title: Email address
explanation: Checks for a practical email shape with one @ and a dot in the domain.
limitations: This is intentionally pragmatic, not a complete RFC email parser; it does not verify that the address exists.

title: HTTP or HTTPS URL
explanation: Requires an HTTP or HTTPS scheme followed by at least one non-space character.
limitations: It does not validate every URL rule or confirm that the host is reachable.

title: IPv4 address
explanation: Validates four decimal octets, each in the range 0–255.
limitations: It does not distinguish private, loopback, multicast, or reserved address ranges.

title: Basic IPv6 address
explanation: Matches the fully expanded eight-group IPv6 notation.
limitations: This educational pattern does not support compressed (::), IPv4-mapped, or zone-indexed IPv6 forms.

title: UUID v4
explanation: Checks the UUID layout plus the version 4 and RFC variant bits.
limitations: It validates format and bits only; it cannot prove uniqueness or how the UUID was generated.

title: Hexadecimal color
explanation: Accepts CSS-style three- or six-digit hexadecimal colors with a leading #.
limitations: It excludes alpha forms such as #RRGGBBAA and functional color notation.

title: ISO calendar date
explanation: Checks the YYYY-MM-DD shape used by ISO-style dates.
limitations: It checks shape, not calendar validity; values such as 2026-99-99 still match.

title: 24-hour time
explanation: Matches hours from 00–23 and minutes from 00–59 in HH:MM format.
limitations: Seconds, time zones, and leap seconds are not included.

title: Signed integer
explanation: Accepts an optional sign followed by one or more decimal digits.
limitations: It does not enforce a numeric range and accepts leading zeroes.

title: Decimal number
explanation: Matches signed whole numbers and decimal values such as 12.5 or .5.
limitations: Scientific notation, locale separators, and numeric range are not supported.

title: Lowercase URL slug
explanation: Allows lowercase words or numbers separated by single hyphens.
limitations: Whether a slug is unique or appropriate for a specific route must be checked separately.

title: ASCII alphanumeric string
explanation: Requires one or more ASCII letters or digits and no punctuation or spaces.
limitations: Unicode letters and underscores are intentionally excluded.

title: Whitespace run
explanation: Finds one or more whitespace characters, including spaces, tabs, and line breaks.
limitations: Whitespace semantics vary by engine and flags; this targets JavaScript behavior.

title: Duplicate spaces
explanation: Finds two or more literal consecutive spaces for cleanup.
limitations: It does not match tabs or newlines; use \s{2,} when those should count.

title: HTML-like tag
explanation: Finds text shaped like an opening or closing HTML tag.
limitations: Do not use regex as an HTML parser; nested structure, quoted > characters, and malformed markup need a parser.

title: JavaScript-style identifier
explanation: Checks the common ASCII shape of a JavaScript identifier.
limitations: It does not reject reserved words and does not cover all Unicode identifier rules.

title: Double-quoted string
explanation: Finds double-quoted strings while allowing escaped characters inside them.
limitations: It is not a full language lexer and may not handle every multiline or templating syntax.

title: Common log level
explanation: Finds common severity labels in application logs.
limitations: Log formats and level names differ between systems.

title: Common access-log line
explanation: Matches the broad shape of a Common Log Format or combined access-log line.
limitations: It checks line shape, not whether methods, dates, status codes, or quoted fields are semantically valid.

title: Semantic version
explanation: Matches the core and optional prerelease/build portions of Semantic Versioning 2.0.
limitations: It does not compare versions or enforce project-specific release rules.

title: MAC address
explanation: Accepts six hexadecimal octets separated by colons or hyphens.
limitations: It does not identify vendor prefixes or guarantee that the address is assigned to a device.

title: Hostname
explanation: Checks labels, hyphen placement, and the maximum hostname length.
limitations: It does not validate DNS resolution, IDN display names, or every application-specific host rule.

title: TCP or UDP port
explanation: Matches an integer from 0 through 65535.
limitations: It does not show whether a port is open or assigned to a particular service.

title: Absolute Unix path
explanation: Checks a slash-prefixed path without null bytes or newline characters.
limitations: Filesystem rules differ by operating system, permissions, and normalization requirements.

title: JSON string token
explanation: Matches a JSON string token with valid escape forms and no raw control characters.
limitations: A token match does not validate a complete JSON document; use a JSON parser for that.

title: Base64 string
explanation: Checks the standard padded Base64 alphabet and grouping.
limitations: It does not decode the value or distinguish arbitrary binary data from text.

title: Hexadecimal number
explanation: Accepts hexadecimal digits with an optional 0x prefix.
limitations: It does not enforce a numeric width or range.

title: US phone number
explanation: Accepts common North American phone formats with an optional country code.
limitations: Phone numbering plans are complex; this does not verify assignment or support every international format.

title: US ZIP code
explanation: Matches five-digit ZIP codes and optional four-digit extensions.
limitations: It checks format only and does not confirm that the ZIP code exists.

title: ISO date-time prefix
explanation: Matches an ISO-like date-time with seconds and an explicit UTC offset.
limitations: Calendar validity and leap seconds are not checked.

title: Simple duration
explanation: Matches a positive numeric duration with a common unit.
limitations: It does not convert units or accept compound durations such as 1h 30m.

title: Quoted CSV field
explanation: Validates one quoted CSV field and permits doubled double-quotes inside it.
limitations: CSV dialects vary; this checks one quoted field only and does not parse a complete row.
